title: hided WebSocket contract
description: Handshake, server frames, close reason codes, path refusal reason codes, and client dispatch events for hided.

snapshot_format.description: Explicitly requests independently retained rest fields, with nested navigator, terminal and status omissions. Missing keeps schema-2 complete-rest replacement. Unknown formats close with schema_mismatch (4003).

have_core.description: The `core_instance` of the daemon frame that came before the snapshot `have_revision` was read from. A core started since (a move, a rollback or an update) answers a whole snapshot whatever `have_revision` says, since each core numbers its own revisions.

have_terminal_sequence.description: The `terminal_sequence` of the last terminal frame a reconnecting client applied. With a delta and the `have_terminal_epoch` of the hub that gave it, it resumes every pane from there (a pane the hub's ring no longer reaches is drawn again from a full frame); a client that kept its terminals and names none, or names it without this hub's epoch, has every pane drawn again; a client given a whole snapshot ignores it.

have_terminal_epoch.description: The `terminal_epoch` of the terminal frame `have_terminal_sequence` came from. Each daemon's hub draws its own, so a page that outlived its daemon names an epoch the new hub does not have and is drawn again whole.

workspaceQuery.description: A pane-scoped query on a capability-authenticated WebSocket. The daemon derives device, pane, and Workspace from the credential and current core projection.

memoryHookAsk.description: `hide workspace memory`: an agent hook's Project Memory, answered by the core from the one store it owns whichever machine the agent runs on, as a workspace_result without a shell. The Project is the one holding the caller pane's attested checkout, read by that checkout's own node; the request never names it. The core's own node and any registered linked device have Memory through that device's node, regardless of connection direction; a link that is down or a helper without a Memory reader refuses immediately with a diagnostic reason, and a disconnected node refuses its callers with hide_unavailable. No store is copied to the device. result is {context, outcome, count?}: context is the Memory text or null, a prompt's cards with their signed receipt and a session start's card index without one, and outcome one of provided (with count), empty, disabled, unavailable, deadline, project_unresolved. The prompt is at most its first 8 KiB, and the core spends at most 1 s on the answer.

linksQuery.description: `hide links`: a read of the link record on a capability-authenticated WebSocket, answered as a workspace_result without a shell. The caller checkout's Project is the scope unless all_projects is set; a target only another Project holds is refused with other_project, and one the record never saw with not_found.

workspaceAction.description: One pane-scoped document or View transition. Repeating the same request ID and command returns its recorded result within the ten-minute retry window.

workspaceResult.description: A pane-scoped request outcome. A successful action result includes context, request_id, changed, view_id, and optionally area_id; a refusal names reason and next_action.

serverFrame.description: snapshot/delta carry the core state; terminal carries pane output beside them, never through the core (see terminalFrame); error answers a malformed client event; directory_list answers a `file_list`, and path_refused answers any event whose path failed its boundary - the $HOME line for `create_workspace` and `clone_repository`, the checkout-root line for `file_list`, `file_open`, `reveal_path`, `file_save`, `file_create`, `dir_create`, `path_rename`, `path_move`, `path_copy`, `path_import`, `path_trash` and `file_bytes` (see directoryList and pathRefused). A `file_list`, `file_open`, `reveal_path`, `file_save`, `file_create`, `dir_create`, `path_rename`, `path_move`, `path_copy`, `path_import` or `path_trash` that names an SSH device in `device_id` never meets this machine's checkout roots: the core accepts it only for the checkout in front on that device and the device's helper confines every path to that checkout's opened root. file_bytes_error answers a `file_bytes` read the daemon could not serve as bytes (see fileBytes). directory_unavailable answers a `file_list` for a checkout on an SSH device that its helper could not list (see directoryUnavailable). directory_changed announces that a watched folder changed, so the client re-reads that one folder (see directoryChanged). attachment_refused answers an `attachment_stage` or `attachment_commit` that could not be staged (see attachments). file_index_result answers a `file_index` query with the ranked checkout paths (see fileIndex). project_target answers a `project_target` probe (see projectTarget and projectTargetResult). clone_target answers a `clone_target` question about where a clone would land (see cloneTarget). daemon is the first frame after a valid handshake and describes the daemon itself (see daemonInfo). agent_notice reaches only a desktop window, and only while one has asked for it with `desktop_notices` (see agentNotice and desktopNoticesPayload). core_move is the core move as the process's supervisor holds it, which every role of the process sends its screens, a node holding its screen from the moment a move is under way, and the only frame a screen gets while a move holds it (`hided/src/core_move/control.rs` `MoveView`); once the move is under way it carries `alias`, the SSH alias the move reaches its other machine by, which a screen that has not drawn the core names that machine by. core_link is where a node's link to its core stands, sent to a screen the node holds while the core cannot draw it: `phase` `connecting`, `updating`, `waiting` or `disconnected`, `machine`, the core machine's name when its hello gave it, else null, and `alias`, the SSH alias the node dials its core by, which a screen that has not drawn the core names instead of an empty machine. `disconnected` is the operator's own end of the link: a screen's `core_link` event {action: `disconnect`} ends it from that machine's node daemon, which records it so a restart keeps it, and {action: `reconnect`} restores it; the node takes that event, and a `core_move` event, even while it holds the screen, and answers a change it could not make with an error frame whose payload is {kind: `core_link`, reason: `not_changed`}. browser_comment answers a window's `browser_comment` event, which turns Comment mode on a browser View on or off: {workspace, display_id, on, reason} names the View in its checkout, since display ids repeat across checkouts, and on: false says the mode ended, with `reason` null when the operator ended it, or why it could not start or went on (`display_busy`, `comment_limit`, `comment_unavailable_here`, or the page's lease failure); while it is on, a frame with `pick` {id, anchor, at} is a place the operator picked in the page, whose screenshot hided holds, one with `open` {id, at} a pin they pressed, `at` being where it shows as fractions of the page's viewport, and one with `dropped` true says the page navigated, to another document or within the same one, and the held pick is gone; the window writes the note itself and adds it with a `browser_comment` event carrying `add` {pick, note}; only an operator's screen (a desktop or web window whose connection its token proved, never a pane's scoped connection) may send it or `view_comment` and `view_feedback_send`. A `file_bytes` read that succeeds is answered with one or more binary frames on the same socket, not a text frame (see fileBytes).

rest_format.description: Present only after snapshot_format negotiation. Each rest field replaces one semantic value; omissions retain, explicit null/empty values clear. Navigator, terminal and status merge their independently revisioned fields. Cursor zero/reset carries all fields.

usage.description: The independently revisioned top-level usage section in a snapshot or delta. Delta omission preserves the previous value; an empty nodes array clears it. A fresh snapshot, including a future-cursor reset, always carries the complete section. Usage-only changes do not resend rest.

terminalFrame.description: Payload of a terminal frame: pane output from the screen-side hub (PRD core-host-node-terminal D-11, D-22), in the order the panes' nodes produced it. One sequence numbers every pane's chunks; terminal_sequence is the client's cursor after this frame, which it names as have_terminal_sequence, with terminal_epoch as have_terminal_epoch, when it reconnects; each daemon's hub has its own epoch, so a cursor resumes only on the hub that gave it. After a whole snapshot the client resets every terminal and is sent a terminal frame with no chunks that gives its new cursor. A pane whose output a client left unsent past 1 MiB, or that a resume cannot reach, sends that client nothing more until a full frame redraws it. Keys go the other way as the `key` event {pane_id or pending_request, bytes_base64}, and a view's grid as `terminal_viewport` {pane_id, cols, rows, new_view}; both reach the pane's node directly and never the core.

daemonInfo.description: Payload of the daemon frame, sent once after a valid handshake and before the first snapshot: what the Settings General tab shows about the daemon. It never carries the token or environment values other than the paths named here; herdr_bin_path and herdr_socket_path are null when the daemon has none. host_id names this daemon host across restarts (`host-` and 32 hex digits, kept in the state directory's `host-id` file); the web shell files unsaved drafts under it, so a draft written against one Hide host is never opened by another that serves the same browser origin. host_name is the name of the machine the daemon runs on, which Settings names as the owner of every value the daemon stores; null when the system does not report one. The daemon also owns the core's one Settings observation flag: a client's `ai_settings` event with `observing` records only that connection's demand, the flag follows the first observer in and the last one out, and a connection that closes releases its demand.

core_instance.description: Drawn fresh each time the core role starts; a client names it as `have_core` when it reconnects.

directoryChanged.description: Payload of a directory_changed frame: the watched folder whose contents changed. The daemon watches the focused checkout's root and its most recently expanded folders, at most 64 in total (the root counts); a change within 200 ms of the last one for the same folder is coalesced into the frame already sent. A client re-reads the one folder this names, which is the Explorer's live refresh without a reload. device_id names the device the folder is on: `local` for the daemon's own machine, polled from opened handles every 200 ms, or an SSH device whose helper stamps the selected device's front checkout root and watched folders (the same 64) every 2 s while its Explorer is showing and its helper is ready; a client ignores a frame for a device it is not showing.

projects.description: Each of the node's projects' last seven days of cost (PRD lane-two-columns B31): absent until the first build succeeds, so a cost not read yet is not drawn as zero (B33); a project that ran no priced call is not listed. Amounts are millionths of a dollar.

projects_failed.description: The latest build of projects failed; the last built list stays. Absent otherwise.

uiStateUsageHints.description: Two fields a `ui_state_update` payload may carry beside the UI state it replaces; the core never persists or echoes them, and an absent field keeps the core's value. usage_window_visible: a shell window is on screen, so the core reads each provider every five minutes. usage_popover_open: the Weekly Usage popover is open; its change from false to true reads again any provider last read more than a minute ago.

focusCheckoutPayload.description: focus_checkout: one admitted focus and optional sidebar disclosure transition. Unknown workspace/checkout refuses the disclosure intent before either value changes.

agentNotice.description: Payload of an agent_notice frame (PRD first-run-onboarding D-09): the daemon judged the agents' latest change the way the phone's push does. Each notice is a root agent that newly needs the operator or has finished; clear lists the tags of notifications to withdraw because the operator has seen that agent. Whether a notification shows, and its words, is the window's and the host's to decide.

status_code.description: The root row's status word code. Optional for older frames.

detail.description: The core's chosen row detail, untranslated; absent or null means the original state-and-project body.

subject.description: A question the core asks on the row for the agent, which the window words in the interface language in place of detail: `plan_review` is a proposed plan of `steps` steps waiting for the operator's review (ask_subject_cause in snapshot-wire-enums.json).

desktopNoticesPayload.description: Payload of the `desktop_notices` client event, accepted only from a desktop window and never sent to the core: wanted says whether this window shows agent notifications. The daemon judges agent changes while any window wants them, and a window's closing withdraws its wish; turning on announces nothing that was already waiting.

sessionSearchCursor.description: Retained History continuation in activity descending, then full native identity ascending order. No offset pagination or raw transcript scan.

sessionSearchOptions.description: History filters apply in the existing links worker before ranking and the 50-session page limit. Project is immutable original project, not today's cwd. Current/archived states require exact core evidence; retained means that state is unconfirmed. Default sources are operator requests only, each retained to 500 characters. Titles and goal flows are opt-in, and flows additionally require summaries enabled.

sessionWorkSearchPayload.description: session_work_search latest-only mailbox request. Blank query browses recent retained sessions; the answer echoes options.request_id and returns up to 50 sessions, up to two matched excerpts per session, total match/request counts and an optional stable tuple cursor. Request hits carry their exact request offset and full device/provider/native-session identity.

interfaceLanguage.description: The core's shared explicit interface language. Null follows each client's primary system language, with English for unsupported languages. Invalid stored values publish en with a diagnostic and remain stored until an explicit edit.

interfaceLanguageSetPayload.description: Payload of interface_language_set. This event alone edits the core preference; ui_state_update never changes it.

agentLogoMode.description: Whether the sidebar, the Sessions list and the tab bar draw an agent's provider logo before its title. Hidden is the default and what a store without the field, or with a value this build does not know, publishes.

agentLogoModeSetPayload.description: Payload of agent_logo_mode_set. This event alone edits the core preference; ui_state_update never changes it, and a mode the event does not name is refused and changes nothing.

paneTurnRowMode.description: How an agent pane draws its turn row, the operator's last request and the agent's answer, over the terminal: one_line keeps every turn and ask on one line and is the default, what a store without the field or with a value this build does not know publishes (with the diagnostic ui_state.pane_turn_row_mode_unknown); two_lines gives the request its own line above the answer; off draws no turn row, an ask rides the pane head as a mark, and a pane with live children keeps its children button.

paneTurnRowModeSetPayload.description: Payload of pane_turn_row_mode_set. This event alone edits the core preference; ui_state_update never changes it, a mode outside paneTurnRowMode is refused and changes nothing, and the current mode again saves nothing.

colorTheme.description: The palette every window draws in, `ui_state.color_theme`: hide is the landing page's Owl Field colors and the default (a store without the field opens hide), neutral the grey chrome. Independent of `ui_state.theme`, which picks light, dark or system. A stored value the core does not know opens hide with the diagnostic ui_state.color_theme_unknown.

colorThemeSetPayload.description: Payload of color_theme_set. This event alone edits the color theme; ui_state_update never changes it, a value outside colorTheme is refused, and the current value again saves nothing.

pathRefusalReason.description: outside_home: the real path is not under $HOME (a symlink target counts) where only a folder inside home may be named: a symlink under home that leads out of it, a parent for Create new project or Clone from URL, or a network share. needs_confirmation: a `create_workspace` names an existing folder by a path written outside $HOME and does not carry `confirmed_outside_home` naming that same path, the operator's confirmation of it; nothing there was read, and the same event with the confirmation is judged by what is there. home_root: $HOME itself, or a folder holding it, cannot be a workspace. project_holds_home: a `create_workspace` names a folder in a Git repository whose root holds $HOME (dotfiles kept in `~/.git`), so the project it would add is home. outside_checkout: the path is not under any registered checkout root, which is the reason an explorer event gets for a path under $HOME that no checkout covers. not_found: nothing exists there. not_a_directory: a file where a directory was needed. not_a_file: a directory where a file's bytes were needed. invalid_path: empty, relative, contains `..` or NUL, or an item name that is empty, `.`, `..`, or holds a `/`. already_exists: a `create_workspace` with `new_folder` names a folder where something other than an empty folder (or one holding only `.git` and `.DS_Store`) already stands.

directoryList.description: Payload of a directory_list frame. kind names the event that asked: a `file_list` lists the children of a folder under a registered checkout root - files and directories, hidden names included, `.git` and a symlink that leaves the root absent, directories first and then the natural name order the macOS Explorer uses. root_path is the real path that was listed. is_directory is what the Explorer draws and opens by. truncated is true past the listing cap. device_id names the machine the listing came from: absent for this daemon's own machine, and an SSH device's id for a `file_list` that named that device, whose paths are that device's and are never read here.

inode.description: The entry's own inode (a link's, not its target's) in a `file_list` answer, as decimal text: the identity a `path_trash` of this row sends back unchanged, so the host moves only the item the operator confirmed. Text because a JSON number reaches the browser as a double, which rounds a 64-bit id past 2^53 (an NTFS file id once its sequence number reaches 32).

directoryUnavailable.description: Payload of a directory_unavailable frame: a `file_list` for a checkout on an SSH device that did not come back as a listing. code says what the Explorer offers next: `not_ready` (no helper connection: consent missing or withdrawn, or the device unreachable; nothing was sent), `busy` (the device's request queue is full; nothing was sent), `unknown` (the request was sent and no answer arrived), or `refused` (the helper answered with a refusal such as a replaced root or a missing folder). reason is the helper's refusal code on `refused` (`not_found`, `permission_denied`, `root_replaced`, ...), null otherwise; the Explorer words code and reason, and the helper's sentence goes to hided's `device.listing_unavailable` log line. root_path is the folder that was asked for.

pathRefused.description: Payload of a path_refused frame: the event kind that carried the path, the path as sent, and why hided did not forward it. A `file_create` or `dir_create` whose name failed the shape check, and a `path_rename` whose new name did, carry that name as the path. A `browser_open`, a `browser_state`, or a `view_layout` navigate whose `url` is a `file:` address is checked like any path: the path it decodes to has to be under a registered checkout root, and the event reaches the core with the `file:` URL of the checked path; a refusal carries the decoded path, or the address as sent when it names another host or does not decode (`invalid_path`).

confirm.description: Only on a `create_workspace` answered `needs_confirmation` whose folder belongs to a project outside home that is not that folder (inside a repository there, or a linked worktree of one): that project's root, the folder the operator is asked about and confirms instead, because a registration adds the project.

cloneTarget.description: Add a project's Clone from URL asks where a clone would land with a `clone_target` event {parent, name} while the operator types, and hided answers this frame without forwarding the event: parent and name as sent, path the canonical folder the clone would create when it may, and reason null or the `$HOME` line's refusal, `already_exists` when anything (a folder, even an empty one or a `.git`-only leftover, a file, a dangling symlink) already holds the name. parent may be home itself or `~`; name is one plain folder name. The `clone_repository` event {url, parent, name} passes the same check, reaches the core with parent rewritten to its canonical spelling, or is answered with path_refused naming `parent/name`. The core then refuses a URL it cannot clone or a name the URL does not give, and reports the clone in the snapshot's repository_clone.

openExternal.description: A browser WebSocket client open_external event is always answered with open_external_result {path, ok:false, reason:"untrusted_client"}, even with a valid token and loopback Origin: localhost may be forwarded from another machine. The bare S3 browser downloads oversized files through file_bytes. The bounded host opener remains implemented for a future transport that can establish local ownership (macOS open, Windows ShellExecuteW default association, Linux xdg-open, or validated absolute HIDE_OPEN_COMMAND); no such transport is present in S3. Windows never passes the pathname through cmd.

openExternalResult.description: Payload of an open_external_result frame: the path supplied by the client, ok false, and reason untrusted_client. The browser WebSocket has no authority to launch the daemon host handler. The retained host opener may later report spawn_failed, over_budget, not_found, or not_openable on a separately authenticated local transport.

attachments.description: The web cannot name a dropped file's path, so it uploads bytes for hided to stage, then commits them. `attachment_stage` {request_id, name, size, clipboard} opens one staged file (an over-cap size is refused at once); the bytes follow as binary frames, each framed like a file_bytes frame but client to server: a 4-byte big-endian header length, the header JSON {request_id, offset, eof}, then that chunk's bytes. `attachment_commit` {request_id, pane_id, bracketed_paste, clipboard, stages} turns the staged files into the one `terminal_attachment` event a shell sends for a batch of paths, with the staged paths as its `paths`; a clipboard commit names no paths, because the image was staged at the path the core reads it from, and hided then reports `terminal_attachment_ready` itself. Caps: 20 MiB per file, 40 MiB and 8 files per batch. hided answers `attachment_refused` {request_id, reason} when a stage or commit fails or exceeds a cap; reason is one of invalid_request_id, invalid_item, too_large, batch_too_large, too_many_files, staging_full, size_mismatch, stage_failed, forward_failed, no_pane, unknown_stage, stage_incomplete. A drop from the file manager into the Explorer uses the same staging: the window stages each file with `attachment_stage`, then sends `path_import` {request_id, root, device_id?, destination, items: [{path, directory, stage?}]} instead of a commit. `request_id` is the 36-character UUID that prefixes each stage id (`<request_id>-<index>`), `path` is the item below the destination folder with `/` between names, and a file names the `stage` that holds its bytes while a folder names none. hided checks the shape (at most 500 items, each name one valid component, a folder with no stage and a file with one; a shape it will not forward is refused as `invalid_item`, a count past the cap as `too_many_files`), judges the destination against the registered roots, turns the stage ids into the staged paths and sends the core its own `path_import`; a client `path_import` is never forwarded as sent. The core reads the staged files and has the checkout's host write the items whole or not at all, naming each `name copy.ext` when its name is taken. The caps are the staging caps (20 MiB per file, 40 MiB per drop) with 500 items instead of 8 files. `path_copy` {root, device_id?, path, destination} copies one item into the folder `destination` of the same checkout the same way, with at most 5000 items and 256 MiB. Each stage id and name is flattened to one path component and refused otherwise; one id and one path identify one stage, and a second stage may not reuse either. A stage whose bytes do not match its declared size is dropped at eof (size_mismatch). Every arriving byte is charged to a 256 MiB staged budget as it lands (a freshly committed file is spared for 60 s, and a full set of them refuses the new stage rather than unlinking one), hided's own attachments directory starts empty on each run, staged files and their directories are mode 0600/0700, a batch names each stage once and its request id must be the 36-character UUID the core requires, a clipboard stage id must be that shape too because the core derives its path from it, a completed stage leaves the open-upload cap, a connection's uncommitted stages are released when it goes, and a cancel never unlinks a file the core was already told about. A clipboard commit must name exactly the one stage that wrote its image, and that stage must have been opened as a clipboard stage; each mode commits only its own root. The shell's own attachment events (terminal_attachment, terminal_attachment_ready, terminal_attachment_action) are the daemon's to send: a client that sends one is answered with an error frame and it never reaches the core. The one exception is the screen relay of a linked node whose core runs on another machine: that node stages its own screens' uploads on its machine, and for one of its own panes it sends terminal_attachment with staged_on naming itself and the paths it staged, which the core pastes without reading or copying them; any other terminal_attachment on a relay is refused the same way. The core still owns the terminal side: its own refusal arrives in the snapshot's async operations.

attachmentRefused.description: Payload of an attachment_refused frame: the request that failed and why nothing was staged.

projectTarget.description: A client `project_target` event asks where Add a project's Create new project would make a folder: {parent, name}. hided answers it on the $HOME line with a project_target frame and never forwards it; it reads the parent and the one name under it and changes nothing on disk. The create itself is a `create_workspace` with `new_folder: true` and `initialize_git: true` whose `path` is the parent and the name joined by `/`: hided checks the parent on the $HOME line (home itself is allowed, since the new folder is under it) and the name as one folder name, refuses anything already standing at the target except an empty folder or one holding only `.git` and `.DS_Store` (what an earlier attempt that failed after making its folder leaves, so a retry continues into it) as already_exists, and forwards the canonical target; the core makes the folder at that literal path before canonicalizing it, so a symlink planted at the name is refused rather than followed, runs `git init` in it, and registers it. A `new_folder` create that names an SSH device is refused by the core.

projectTargetResult.description: Payload of a project_target frame: the parent and name as sent; the canonical parent and its `~` spelling when the parent resolved; the canonical target when the name was checked too; whether an empty leftover folder is already there and will be used; and the path refusal reason the create would get, or null. An empty name checks the parent alone.

fileIndex.description: A client `file_index` event asks for the files of a registered checkout that match a query: {root, query}. The daemon walks the checkout once, honoring .gitignore (and .git/info/exclude and the global ignore file) without a git process, caps the index at 50,000 files, and answers with a file_index_result frame: {root_path, query, files: [{path, relative_path}], truncated, indexing}. `files` is ranked by the palette's fuzzy score, best first, at most 80; `path` is absolute so the client can open it, `relative_path` is what the palette shows. The first query for a root answers `indexing: true` while the walk runs; `truncated` marks a checkout whose index hit the cap. A root that is not a registered checkout is the usual path_refused frame with kind file_index. With `device_id` naming an SSH device, `root` is a checkout the core's catalog carries for that device, the walk is that device's helper's, `path` is spelled on that device, and a walk the helper could not make is answered with `unavailable` naming why; the next query walks again.

fileIndexResult.description: Payload of a file_index_result frame: the device and root that were searched, the query, the ranked files, whether the index is truncated, whether the walk is still running, and why a device walk was unavailable, as a code the palette words (`host.<code>` for the helper's refusal, `link.not_connected`, `link.busy` or `link.unknown`); the helper's sentence goes to hided's `device.index_unavailable` log line.

fileBytes.description: A client `file_bytes` event asks for a regular file's bytes under a registered checkout root: {request_id, path, offset, length}. `length` null or absent reads to the end of the file; `offset` defaults to 0. The daemon answers with one or more binary frames, each framed as a 4-byte big-endian header length, the header JSON as UTF-8, then that chunk's bytes. The header is {type: "file_bytes", request_id, path, offset, total, eof}: offset is where this chunk starts in the file, total is the file's whole size, and eof marks the last frame. A read past MAX_FILE_BYTES (256 MiB) or a disk failure is answered with a file_bytes_error text frame instead: {request_id, path, reason} where reason is too_large or read_failed; a device read that a newer one from the same client ended (at most two run per client) is answered with reason superseded. A path that fails the boundary is the usual path_refused frame with kind file_bytes. With `device_id` naming an SSH device and `root` a checkout the core's catalog carries for it, `path` is spelled under that root on the device and the device's helper reads it one bounded range at a time; a file that changes between ranges ends the read as read_failed.

fileBytesError.description: Payload of a file_bytes_error frame: the read that failed and why.

feature.description: The closed group a router request's feature id falls into; an id outside the list is other.

providers.description: Provider ids of the models that answered, for the row's marks.

usageHideAiDay.description: Hide's own background AI on one day. Its known part is already inside the day's amount.

amount.description: The sum of features. A lower bound (cost.partial) when unknown_calls is not zero.

share_basis_points.description: The known Hide AI new tokens over the day's new tokens.

unknown_calls.description: Attempts that were submitted and reported no usage. A count of calls, never tokens, so it is in no amount.

hide_ai.description: Only the all-agents range carries it, on a day Hide AI was counted; an agent's own range is that agent's sessions.

calendar_start.description: Inclusive civil-date calendar bound owned by the core.

calendar_end.description: Inclusive civil-date calendar bound owned by the core.

days.description: Sparse recorded days, including calls with zero new tokens. The shell fills omitted dates inside the inclusive calendar bounds.

hide_ai_since.description: The first retained day Hide AI was counted on; no earlier day is. Only the all-agents range carries it.

usageModelDay.description: One recorded day/agent/model contribution on the core node. Hide AI is already in all-agent totals. Per-model call counts are reports, not backend attempts.

models.description: Newest recorded model/day contributions inside the year calendar. Absent on older daemons; unknown model names are null. No model is inferred from aggregate totals.

models_limited.description: Model detail exceeded 4096 rows. Listed contributions are partial; the independent daily and period totals are unchanged.
